All code is base `R`. Every number quoted on the Session 25 slides can be reproduced here.

## Why not many t tests

```{r}
1 - 0.95^c(3, 6, 15)       # P(at least one false positive): 3 tests, 6 tests, 15 tests (k = 6)
choose(6, 2)               # 15 pairs of 6 groups
```

## Small example by hand

```{r}
y <- c(12, 14, 11, 15,  16, 18, 15, 19,  20, 17, 21, 22)
g <- factor(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 4))
ybar_i <- tapply(y, g, mean); ybar <- mean(y); n_i <- table(g)
SSTr <- sum(n_i * (ybar_i - ybar)^2)     # 98.67
SSE  <- sum((y - ybar_i[g])^2)           # 34
c(SSTr, SSE, SSTr + SSE)
F <- (SSTr / 2) / (SSE / 9); F           # 13.06
qf(0.95, 2, 9); pf(F, 2, 9, lower.tail = FALSE)
summary(aov(y ~ g))
```

## Your turn 1 and exit ticket (illustrative numbers)

```{r}
Ftab <- function(SSTr, SSE, k, N) {
  F <- (SSTr / (k - 1)) / (SSE / (N - k))
  c(F = F, crit = qf(0.95, k - 1, N - k), p = pf(F, k - 1, N - k, lower.tail = FALSE),
    eta2 = SSTr / (SSTr + SSE))
}
Ftab(84, 192, 4, 20)     # F = 2.33, crit 3.24, p = 0.113, eta2 = 0.30
Ftab(120, 300, 5, 35)    # F = 3.00, crit 2.69, p = 0.034, eta2 = 0.29
pf(106 / 25, 3, 36, lower.tail = FALSE)   # Your turn 2: p = 0.0115
```

## Chick growth: full analysis

```{r}
fit <- aov(weight ~ feed, data = chickwts)
summary(fit)                              # F = 15.37, p = 5.9e-10
s <- summary(fit)[[1]]; s[1, 2] / sum(s[, 2])   # eta^2 = 0.54
tapply(chickwts$weight, chickwts$feed, function(v) c(n = length(v), mean = mean(v), sd = sd(v)))
qf(0.95, 5, 65)                           # 2.36
sqrt(s[2, 3])                             # pooled sd 54.9
# interval for the casein mean
323.58 + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, 65) * sqrt(s[2, 3] / 12)
```

## Diagnostics

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)); plot(fit, which = 1:2); par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
bartlett.test(weight ~ feed, data = chickwts)        # p = 0.66
dev <- abs(chickwts$weight - ave(chickwts$weight, chickwts$feed, FUN = median))
summary(aov(dev ~ feed, data = chickwts))            # Brown-Forsythe, p = 0.59
shapiro.test(resid(fit))
max(tapply(chickwts$weight, chickwts$feed, sd)) / min(tapply(chickwts$weight, chickwts$feed, sd))  # 1.68
```

Insect sprays: unequal variances.

```{r}
bartlett.test(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)               # p < 0.001
summary(aov(sqrt(count) ~ spray, data = InsectSprays))
bartlett.test(sqrt(count) ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)         # p = 0.59
oneway.test(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)                 # Welch: F = 36.07
oneway.test(weight ~ feed, data = chickwts)
kruskal.test(weight ~ feed, data = chickwts)
```

## After a significant F

```{r}
tk <- TukeyHSD(fit); round(tk$feed, 3)
sum(tk$feed[, "p adj"] < 0.05)                     # 8 of 15
qtukey(0.95, 6, 65)                                # 4.15
pw <- pairwise.t.test(chickwts$weight, chickwts$feed, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni", pool.sd = TRUE)
sum(pw$p.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)               # 8 as well
0.05 / 15
```

## F = t^2 for two groups

```{r}
d <- droplevels(subset(chickwts, feed %in% c("horsebean", "linseed")))
tt <- t.test(weight ~ feed, data = d, var.equal = TRUE); tt$statistic^2   # 8.61
summary(aov(weight ~ feed, data = d))
qf(0.95, 1, 20); qt(0.975, 20)^2                                          # 4.35
# Your turn 4
(-2.5)^2; qf(0.95, 1, 14); pf(6.25, 1, 14, lower.tail = FALSE)            # 6.25, 4.60, 0.025
```
